name: Cold Water First
tagline: You practise alone so that strangers can laugh together.
epigraph: People came to watch the fire. This is what was underneath it.
glassware: a small heatproof glass tumbler (about 300 ml), warmed with hot water first
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v2) and 4-gram check: clean against every pour and the registry, no "we" (only "We don't know"), no "yours" for the drink. Echoes moved off: *Serviceable*'s "long strip of lemon peel", *Standing By*'s "that's the part of", *Instead*'s "part of you people", *Hoping You'd Come*'s "the historian David Wondrich", the Genie's "for once", *Their Night*'s "This time", *Off Duty*'s "sit down". The trap "it looks effortless" (*Not Too Polite*, *Nothing to It*, *Half a Rim*) and *Anyway*'s laugh-at-the-flop kept out. The three he/his warnings are Jerry Thomas and the Chicago bartender, accepted by Wren (r5). History 234 of 470 words in yours (49.8%, Hester). ✓

names_note: **Cold Water First**, the room's pick (all three): Thomas's one piece of advice for the throw, and the reading's proposal (practise first, and with someone). Tomás conceded *Under the Blaze* (r5); Wren: it names the drink, not the person, and repeats the epigraph. Also considered: *Nobody's Stranger*, *For Some Time*, *Under the Fire*, *Behind the Cards*, *Two Strangers*.
open_items: **Never thrown:** the drink is the hot Scotch Whisky Skin under the Blazer ("merely a Scotch Whisky Skin", Wondrich, pdf 141), never lit and never poured between mugs, hot or unlit. The fire stays in the story.

**Whose is what:** Scotch and Irish "mixed" is the 1863 recipe as reprinted in 1867 (the 1863 book is lost); "half and half" and the water ratio are Wondrich's readings. Our measures follow the 1862 Skin's half-filled tumbler; the 14 g demerara is Tomás's balance call (the Skin has no sugar). Why Thomas mixed the whiskies isn't known; the reading tells it as "my guess".

**The cover:** Thomas's "cover with cup" most likely put the flame out (Hester's inference, matching Oxford's "snuff each mug"); the saucer's job here (keeping lemon oil and smoke in) is ours, told as "kept the cover and given it a new job".

**Caol Ila:** "the distillery whose malt Thomas kept in his cellar" (in barrels, Wondrich pdf 137); the first official single malt was bottled in 2002 (Oxford pdf 402), so never "the whisky he poured". The 43% is dated 2026-10-01.

**The crowd:** the 1883 Chicago line is a sneer ("seldom called for over a first-class bar"), told in the reading as the sneerer's; "jays" stays out. The Kansas City burn and Matt Higgins stay in the dossier only.
**No Flavor Matrix spark:** consulted and set aside (sherry vinegar is *Fair Measure*'s; sage and caraway are taken; nuts are a veto). The interest is the book's own split base.
**Dossier note (Hester):** Wren's working table "Facts used" still shows two struck questions ("almost the only secret", "a classic hot drink"); superseded by X6 and X8/A, not claims.
